correctness.rationale: Walsh diagonalization yields an exact six-class rational expression on Q5. Each numerator is a positive monomial factor times a strictly positive polynomial on h>0: the first five have coefficientwise positivity and the sixth has two transformed polynomials with exactly positive coefficients covering the half-line. Positive denominator factors and the cube-lift identity transfer this to dimensions 1..4. Direct exact rational arithmetic yields Q6 negative antipodal entry at h=1/6, with early h^6 and late constant-mode signs; CHECKER.py replay passes all identities. Independent direct Q3 matrix inversion cross-checks 64 entries. Limits: finite tests alone are not general proof; continuous proof uses exact polynomial positivity.

evidence: The published seven-vertex minimum is a universal positive result through graph order six plus a specific P7 counterexample; Q5 order 32 and Q6 order 64 are not logical corollaries.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Neither the general small-order result nor semigroup convergence implies all-step positivity in dimension five. A negative entry on P7 also does not imply negativity for a cube at a given dimension, since induced subgraphs do not generally preserve rational inverse entries. The new theorem proves both Q5 positivity and a Q6 witness from scratch.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The claim is equivalently complete positivity of the inverse of a cubic polynomial in the Q_d Laplacian at every positive h, or nonnegativity of all Hamming-distance Walsh coefficients. It is not the all-graph order threshold, an explicit Taylor step, or a Radau IIA stability function. No observed same-family result settles the exact dimensions 5 and 6.

value.rationale: Positivity preservation is an essential structural requirement for heat-flow probabilities and maximum principles not guaranteed by L-stability. The result resolves a natural all-timestep dimension boundary for one fixed standard Padé integrator: Q5 has 32 vertices and a nontrivial degree-10 positive polynomial certificate, whereas Q6 has 64 vertices and a concrete negative entry with sign reentry. It is more than a trivial finite-step table or small parameter tweak.
